text:
maria.chen: Heads-up — saw an authz regression right after the KMS rekey job finished last night. Service tokens from a legacy pool are able to call the embeddings route even though the per-route allowlist for those tokens is empty. Repro in prod-c1. @kevin @dina

kevin: Noted. Can you paste the simplest repro/log snippet and which token IDs are showing it?

maria.chen: Minimal log excerpt (redacted ids):
```
[2026-03-19T22:11:08Z] authz.check token=svc-acc-42 route=/v1/embeddings -> allowed=true reason=fallthrough_legacy_map
[2026-03-19T22:11:08Z] token.meta { id: "svc-acc-42", tags: [], kms_key_tag: null }
[2026-03-19T22:11:08Z] route.allowlist []
```
This is surprising because svc-acc-42 previously had no embedding permission. After rekey the token.meta shows kms_key_tag=null for several tokens.

ops-bot: deploy:km-rekey finished for region prod-c1 2026-03-19T21:50:02Z (job-id: rekey-2026-03-19-21-30).

dina: initial hypothesis — during the rewrap we dropped per-token KMS metadata tag used by authz to map token->scopes. The authz service has a fallback that looks up legacy allowlist mappings when tag missing; bug is the fallback treats missing tag as "legacy:true" instead of deny. I'll dig in.

raj: I reproduced locally by simulating rewrap that clears `kms_key_tag`. The authz code path in `authz/eval.go` does something like:
```
if token.KmsTag == "" {
  return legacyLookup(token.ID) // BUG: should be deny or require explicit allow flag
}
```
legacyLookup returns permissions for old-service-tokens which explains why embeddings were allowed.

kevin: Oof. That's the permissive default we were scared of. Immediate mitigations: 1) block the few impacted token IDs at the edge ACL; 2) flip feature flag `allow_legacy_map=true` -> `false` in prod-safety for authz; 3) purge authz cache so stale entries don't persist. I'm doing 1+2 now.

maria.chen: Thanks. FYI affected tokens so far: svc-acc-42, svc-acc-99, svc-acc-314. They belong to a vendor integration that we scheduled to rotate anyway.

julie: I pushed an emergency ACL rule to block those three tokens (edge rule id: deny-3422). Also toggled `allow_legacy_map=false` in prod-c1 via runway feature flip (flagid: ff/authz/legacy-map).

ops-bot: feature-flag:ff/authz/legacy-map -> false (actor: julie)

raj: With the flag off, the authz service now returns deny for the repro requests. I also ran a job to rehydrate tags from the KMS metadata backup for tokens where it exists, but several tokens truly lost metadata during rewrap and will need full key rotation.

kevin: Next steps (owners):
- raj: open PR to change default fallback behavior to deny and add audit metric when fallback is hit (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12345)
- dina: add end-to-end test for rewrap -> authz tag-preservation and negative test for missing tag = deny
- julie: create runbook step to block tokens when rewrap observed (short-term) and notify customers impacted
- maria.chen: coordinate token rotations with the vendor and record timeline for postmortem

maria.chen: I already emailed vendor POC and requested rotation within 24h. We will also offer to assist with re-issuing tokens and updating KMS metadata.

raj: Opening the PR now — changes are minimal: fallback returns deny and we emit `authz.fallback_legacy=true` metric when it triggers so ops can alert. Also adding a one-off migration to mark tokens with missing tags as suspect in the DB.

dina: For RCA items to include in postmortem: why metadata dropped during rewrap (investigate rewrap worker ordering), why the authz fallback default was permissive (bad safety assumption), and missing QA test for rewrap+authz.

kevin: Impact summary for postmortem: brief window (~20m) where legacy tokens could access embeddings; small set of customer tokens (3 known, scan in progress). No evidence of exfil/logging beyond allowed operations.

julie: I've opened a support ticket for the vendor accounts and set an internal alert to surface any additional tokens hit by fallback legacy map in the last 24h. Ticket: SUP-2026-778

maria.chen: Good work. After PR merge let's schedule a short oncall play to validate flag flips and add a smoke test for per-route enforcement after any KMS rekey.

kevin: Agreed. I'll take postmortem owner. We should target an ops runbook update and deploy the code fix in the next patch release (T+2 days), keep the feature flag as an emergency toggle for 72h, then remove fallback code after customers rotated.

ops-bot: incident-note created (id: in-342210) severity: P2

maria.chen: Thanks everyone. I'll add the customer communication draft to the ticket and attach logs.

julie: One more — adding CPI (compliance) to the loop to see if we need to notify auditors. cc @compliance-team

kevin: Please also add a note in the release notes and change-log about the hardening.

maria.chen: Will do.
